chant.titulo: Where Are You Going to Stay?
chant.letra:
[Leader]
Where are you going to stay?
[Kids]
In a tent! Beside the water!

[Leader]
And you?
[Kids]
In a hotel! We're going to book a room!

[Leader]
And you?
[Kids]
On a farm! With Sofía's grandfather!

[Leader]
And the best one of all?
[Kids]
The lighthouse! The lighthouse!

[All]
Caravan, suitcase, guest and view —
pack it up, we're going too!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
We're going to book a room in August,
we're going to take the northern train.
The suitcase is already open
and it's going to fill again.

[Chorus]
A tent, a farm, a caravan,
a hotel with a view!
But the room up in the lighthouse
is the one I'm going to choose!

[Verse 2]
The guest book by the window
has a hundred names inside.
We're going to add another
on the night we stay and hide.

[Chorus]
A tent, a farm, a caravan,
a hotel with a view!
But the room up in the lighthouse
is the one I'm going to choose!

[Bridge]
'Going to' is a plan you made,
not a wish that's on parade.

[Chorus]
A tent, a farm, a caravan,
a hotel with a view!
But the room up in the lighthouse
is the one I'm going to choose!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What did you ride?
[Kids]
The big wheel! And the roller coaster!

[Leader]
What did you eat?
[Kids]
Candy floss! Pink candy floss!

[Leader]
Did you scream?
[Kids]
We screamed! We all screamed!

[Leader]
And what happened at the end?
[Kids]
We won! Maya won a balloon!

[All]
Ticket, queue and spin and fell —
we were there and we can tell!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
We bought the tickets at eleven,
we stood in the longest queue.
The big wheel took us up so slowly
that the whole town came in view.

[Chorus]
We rode, we ate, we screamed, we spun,
we fell about and then we won!
Candy floss and a red balloon —
and it was over far too soon!

[Verse 2]
The roller coaster took our voices,
Diego lost his hat.
Oliver said he wasn't frightened
and nobody believed that.

[Chorus]
We rode, we ate, we screamed, we spun,
we fell about and then we won!
Candy floss and a red balloon —
and it was over far too soon!

[Bridge]
None of these verbs takes '-ed'.
They change instead — use your head.

[Chorus]
We rode, we ate, we screamed, we spun,
we fell about and then we won!
Candy floss and a red balloon —
and it was over far too soon!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
Which way first?
[Kids]
North! Twenty steps north!

[Leader]
And then?
[Kids]
East! Cross the stream!

[Leader]
And then?
[Kids]
South! Past the cave!

[Leader]
And where do we dig?
[Kids]
Where the cross is! X marks it!

[All]
West and map and step and secret —
keep it quiet, don't you leak it!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
Twenty steps towards the north,
then east across the stream.
The map is old and torn in half
and half of it's a dream.

[Chorus]
North and south and east and west,
count the steps and cross the line!
Dig where the two lines meet —
the treasure's yours and mine!

[Verse 2]
Ingrid holds the compass,
Maya holds the spade.
The secret's only good
while the secret's being made.

[Chorus]
North and south and east and west,
count the steps and cross the line!
Dig where the two lines meet —
the treasure's yours and mine!

[Bridge]
The treasure wasn't in the ground.
It was the afternoon we found.

[Chorus]
North and south and east and west,
count the steps and cross the line!
Dig where the two lines meet —
the treasure's yours and mine!

46.unidad: In the future, I might be…

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What will you be?
[Kids]
I might be a vet! I might!

[Leader]
Are you sure?
[Kids]
Not sure! Perhaps! Maybe!

[Leader]
And you?
[Kids]
I may be an inventor! Or a writer!

[Leader]
Is it possible?
[Kids]
Everything is possible!

[All]
Farmer, designer, might and may —
nobody knows, and that's okay!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
I might be a vet, I'm not sure yet,
I may be a designer too.
Perhaps I'll be an inventor
like the one my grandad knew.

[Chorus]
Might and may and perhaps and maybe —
it's possible, that's all!
Nobody knows at eleven
and nobody has to call!

[Verse 2]
Oliver may be a writer,
Maya might be all of them.
The farmer and the designer
both start out the same.

[Chorus]
Might and may and perhaps and maybe —
it's possible, that's all!
Nobody knows at eleven
and nobody has to call!

[Bridge]
'Will' is sure and 'might' is open.
Open is a better door.

[Chorus]
Might and may and perhaps and maybe —
it's possible, that's all!
Nobody knows at eleven
and nobody has to call!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
If it rains on Saturday…
[Kids]
we'll stay inside!

[Leader]
If it's sunny…
[Kids]
we'll have the picnic outside!

[Leader]
If the bus is late…
[Kids]
we'll walk instead!

[Leader]
And if everything goes wrong?
[Kids]
We'll still go! We'll still go!

[All]
Plan and bring and cancel, when —
if it rains, we'll plan again!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
If it rains on Saturday
we'll move the picnic in.
If the wind gets up at midday
we'll begin again.

[Chorus]
If it rains, we'll stay inside,
if it's dry, we're going out!
Bring a coat and bring a plan —
and we'll still go, no doubt!

[Verse 2]
When it rains here it rains sideways,
that is simply what it does.
We don't cancel for the weather —
we just change the plan because.

[Chorus]
If it rains, we'll stay inside,
if it's dry, we're going out!
Bring a coat and bring a plan —
and we'll still go, no doubt!

[Bridge]
'When' is certain. 'If' is not.
One small word decides a lot.

[Chorus]
If it rains, we'll stay inside,
if it's dry, we're going out!
Bring a coat and bring a plan —
and we'll still go, no doubt!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
A person…
[Kids]
WHO! The person WHO helps!

[Leader]
A thing…
[Kids]
WHICH! The thing WHICH opens doors!

[Leader]
A place…
[Kids]
WHERE! The place WHERE we met!

[Leader]
Can you guess my riddle?
[Kids]
Describe it! Say what it means!

[All]
Who for people, which for things —
where for places: three small strings!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
The thing which opens every door,
the place where all the boats come in,
the person who remembers names —
guess them all and you can win.

[Chorus]
Who for a person, which for a thing,
where for a place you know!
Three small words that join two halves
and make the meaning grow!

[Verse 2]
A riddle is a sentence
with the answer taken out.
Describe it well enough
and nobody's in doubt.

[Chorus]
Who for a person, which for a thing,
where for a place you know!
Three small words that join two halves
and make the meaning grow!

[Bridge]
The person who helps when nobody sees
is the person this song means.

[Chorus]
Who for a person, which for a thing,
where for a place you know!
Three small words that join two halves
and make the meaning grow!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
Do you like it?
[Kids]
Yes, I do! Yes, I do!

[Leader]
Has she finished?
[Kids]
No, she hasn't! Not yet!

[Leader]
Can they hear us?
[Kids]
Yes, they can! Loud and clear!

[Leader]
Was it correct?
[Kids]
Yes, it was! One point!

[All]
Question, answer, buzzer, round —
quick and short, that's the sound!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
The game show has a buzzer
and the round begins at nine.
The question's short, the answer's shorter
and the point is yours or mine.

[Chorus]
Yes, I do. No, she hasn't.
Yes, they can. No, it wasn't!
Quick and correct beats long and wrong —
and the winner's who was honest!

[Verse 2]
Don't say the whole thing over,
just the little part that counts.
'Yes, I have' is a full answer
in the smallest possible amounts.

[Chorus]
Yes, I do. No, she hasn't.
Yes, they can. No, it wasn't!
Quick and correct beats long and wrong —
and the winner's who was honest!

[Bridge]
Repeat the helping verb, not all of it.
That's the trick, and that is it.

[Chorus]
Yes, I do. No, she hasn't.
Yes, they can. No, it wasn't!
Quick and correct beats long and wrong —
and the winner's who was honest!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
Quick —
[Kids]
QUICKLY!

[Leader]
Slow —
[Kids]
SLOWLY!

[Leader]
Quiet —
[Kids]
QUIETLY!

[Leader]
Loud —
[Kids]
LOUDLY!

[Leader]
And good?
[Kids]
WELL! Not 'goodly'! WELL!

[All]
Carefully, easily, happily, badly —
suddenly it's easy, gladly!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
She reads quickly, he reads slowly,
they both read carefully.
Oliver sings loudly
and Maya sings quietly.

[Chorus]
Add the '-ly' and say it: how?
Quickly, slowly, happily!
But 'good' becomes 'well', not 'goodly' —
and 'fast' just stays as 'fast', you see!

[Verse 2]
He did it badly on the Monday,
he did it easily by Thursday.
Suddenly it made sense —
and that is how it works.

[Chorus]
Add the '-ly' and say it: how?
Quickly, slowly, happily!
But 'good' becomes 'well', not 'goodly' —
and 'fast' just stays as 'fast', you see!

[Bridge]
An adjective describes a thing.
An adverb tells you how it's done.

[Chorus]
Add the '-ly' and say it: how?
Quickly, slowly, happily!
But 'good' becomes 'well', not 'goodly' —
and 'fast' just stays as 'fast', you see!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What's your surname?
[Kids]
Say it! Spell it!

[Leader]
How old are you?
[Kids]
Eleven! Twelve! Say your age!

[Leader]
What's your hometown?
[Kids]
Say where you're from!

[Leader]
What's your favourite subject?
[Kids]
Say it and say WHY!

[All]
Hobby, family, pet and wish —
that's yourself, and that's the list!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
What's your surname? How do you spell it?
How old were you last July?
What's your hometown, what's your hobby?
Say it — and then say why.

[Chorus]
All about you, all about you,
and the 'why' is half the answer!
Family, pet and favourite subject —
you're the only one who has them!

[Verse 2]
If you had one wish, they ask you,
and you never know quite what.
So you say the honest thing
and that's the best you've got.

[Chorus]
All about you, all about you,
and the 'why' is half the answer!
Family, pet and favourite subject —
you're the only one who has them!

[Bridge]
A short answer stops the talk.
A reason keeps it going.

[Chorus]
All about you, all about you,
and the 'why' is half the answer!
Family, pet and favourite subject —
you're the only one who has them!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What's the opposite of 'noisy'?
[Kids]
Quiet! Quiet!

[Leader]
What rhymes with 'sea'?
[Kids]
Tree! Free! Me!

[Leader]
How many vowels in 'meaning'?
[Kids]
Four! Count them!

[Leader]
And where do you check?
[Kids]
The dictionary! Always!

[All]
Spelling, letter, sound and pair —
alphabet and meaning there!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
A rhyme is two words at the end
that finish with one sound.
An opposite is the far side
of the very same ground.

[Chorus]
Look it up, look it up,
the dictionary knows!
Spelling, meaning, sound and letter —
that's the way it goes!

[Verse 2]
A vowel holds the word together,
the rest just gives it shape.
Find the pair, then find the meaning,
and no word can escape.

[Chorus]
Look it up, look it up,
the dictionary knows!
Spelling, meaning, sound and letter —
that's the way it goes!

[Bridge]
A word you looked up once
is a word you own for life.

[Chorus]
Look it up, look it up,
the dictionary knows!
Spelling, meaning, sound and letter —
that's the way it goes!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
Read the instructions!
[Kids]
First! Always first!

[Leader]
Look at the example!
[Kids]
It shows you what to do!

[Leader]
How many times do you hear it?
[Kids]
Twice! You hear it twice!

[Leader]
And if you miss a gap?
[Kids]
Relax! Wait for the second time!

[All]
Pencil, check the spelling, colour —
number every gap and breathe!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
Read the instructions to the end,
the example shows the way.
Take a pencil, not a pen,
in case you change what you say.

[Chorus]
You will hear it twice — relax!
The second time is yours!
Check the spelling, check the number,
check the gap, and pause!

[Verse 2]
If you miss it, leave it empty,
don't go chasing what has gone.
The next one starts in two seconds
and you need to still be on.

[Chorus]
You will hear it twice — relax!
The second time is yours!
Check the spelling, check the number,
check the gap, and pause!

[Bridge]
A colour word must be spelt right.
That's the one they always check.

[Chorus]
You will hear it twice — relax!
The second time is yours!
Check the spelling, check the number,
check the gap, and pause!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What do you read first?
[Kids]
The title! Always the title!

[Leader]
What do you do with the key words?
[Kids]
Underline them! Underline!

[Leader]
How do you spell it?
[Kids]
Copy from the text! Exactly!

[Leader]
And the word limit?
[Kids]
Count them! Don't go over!

[All]
Capital letter, full stop, time —
answer sheet and every line!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
Read the title before the text,
it tells you what it's for.
Underline the words that matter
in each paragraph and more.

[Chorus]
Copy it exactly from the text,
capital letter, full stop!
Watch the word limit, watch the time,
and fill the answer sheet, don't stop!

[Verse 2]
If a word is in the passage,
you don't have to guess the spelling.
Copy it exactly as it stands —
that's a mark they're always giving.

[Chorus]
Copy it exactly from the text,
capital letter, full stop!
Watch the word limit, watch the time,
and fill the answer sheet, don't stop!

[Bridge]
Five minutes at the end to check
is worth ten minutes at the start.

[Chorus]
Copy it exactly from the text,
capital letter, full stop!
Watch the word limit, watch the time,
and fill the answer sheet, don't stop!

chant.letra:
[Leader]
What's today?
[Kids]
The ceremony! The graduation!

[Leader]
What do you get?
[Kids]
A certificate! With our name!

[Leader]
How do you feel?
[Kids]
Proud! Together! Proud!

[Leader]
And what do we say?
[Kids]
Congratulations! Congratulations!

[All]
Remember the adventure, say goodbye —
the future's out there, standing by!

cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
The hall is full, the lights are on,
the ceremony starts at four.
Your certificate has got your name
and everything you did before.

[Chorus]
Congratulations, all of you!
Proud and loud and here together!
Remember every adventure —
and this one lasts forever!

[Verse 2]
Ingrid took us up the mountain,
Diego asked the questions.
Maya named the rivers
and Oliver made the songs.

[Chorus]
Congratulations, all of you!
Proud and loud and here together!
Remember every adventure —
and this one lasts forever!

[Bridge]
Goodbye is not the end of it.
The future's just the next bit.

[Chorus]
Congratulations, all of you!
Proud and loud and here together!
Remember every adventure —
and this one lasts forever!
